description: Found 2026-07-31 by sentinel sweep of anonymize_result_payload. The public export pseudonymizes usernames ('user'/'username'/'userid' -> user_<hash> via anonymization_specs.yaml identifier_keys) so published results never carry real usernames - but 'pg_user' compacts to 'pguser', which matches NOTHING in identifier_keys, so a real connection username is published verbatim. Same for 'tenant_id' ('tenantid' - an Azure AD tenant identifier). Driven proof: anonymize_result_payload({'platform_metadata':{'platform_raw_config':{'pg_user':'PGUSER-SENTINEL','tenant_id':'TENANT-SENTINEL'}}}) returns both sentinels verbatim. pg_user is DuckLake's postgres username key (ducklake.py:55 keeps it out of ducklake's own metadata, but any other payload path carrying pg_user is exposed). Related-but-distinct: internal-result-metadata-exports-connection-usernames covers the INTERNAL path's username handling; this item is the PUBLIC path's identifier-key coverage.
